title: October 12, 2014: a cyclone with 185 km/h winds hit India's coast. It killed 116 people - not tens of thousands.

sources.text: India Meteorological Department (RSMC New Delhi) - Cyclone Hudhud report

caption:
October 12, 2014: a cyclone with 185 km/h winds hit India's coast. It killed 116 people - not tens of thousands.

With sustained winds near 185 km/h and gusts to 260 km/h, Hudhud was the first cyclone to cross the Visakhapatnam coast in October since 1985 - and by every historical measure, a storm of this strength should have killed far more people than it did.

IMD forecasting and coordinated evacuation drills - built up since the 1999 Odisha super-cyclone killed nearly 10,000 people with far less warning - let authorities move almost half a million people out of Hudhud's path in time.

Fifteen decades after a cyclone with no warning system killed tens of thousands in Calcutta, a cyclone nearly as strong killed 116 - because the warning system finally existed.
